title: Billing Disputes on Personal Credit Cards: Claim, Notice Period and Resolution
content:
### What a billing dispute is

A billing dispute on a card under Personal Credit Cards is the cardholder's own claim about one posted purchase, cash advance or balance transfer. The agent registers it in the bank's dispute records with a status of submitted and a notice date equal to the day the cardholder gave notice. Disputes on fees, interest or payments are handled as fee or interest reversals, not here.

### The notice period

The notice must be given within the tier's notice window in calendar days after the statement on which the charge first appeared. Count calendar days with the day after the charge's statement date as day 1; the notice qualifies when the notice date is on or before the statement date plus the tier's notice window in days. The statement date of the disputed charge, held in the bank's own card records, is the anchor, and the boundary day itself qualifies.

*Boundary illustration.* On a tier whose notice window is 60 calendar days, a charge first appearing on a statement dated the 10th of a month is in notice until and including the 60th day counted from the 11th; notice given on that 60th day qualifies, and notice given on the next day does not.

### The temporary credit

That a temporary credit of the claimed amount, never more than the charge, is posted as a temporary dispute credit on the day a qualifying dispute is registered is a basis no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the size of that credit. Only a dispute whose status is submitted can receive a temporary credit, the status being read from the dispute record before the credit is posted. Each dispute receives at most one temporary credit: where a temporary dispute credit already stands for that dispute, no second one is posted.

### While the dispute is open

While a dispute is open, the disputed amount is not counted toward the minimum payment, and no late fee or interest accrues on it.

### Resolution

When the dispute is resolved for the cardholder the temporary credit becomes final with no new entry, or, if no temporary credit was posted, a final credit is posted as a final dispute credit; fees and interest billed on the disputed charge are reversed. That a temporary credit may be rebilled only when the dispute's status is resolved against the cardholder or withdrawn, for the full temporary credit, with the temporary credit as its source item, is likewise a basis no longer in force, superseded by the current basis for the amount rebilled. A merchant credit for the same purchase that posts while the dispute is open resolves it for the cardholder up to the credit amount; the temporary credit is then rebilled for the part the merchant credit covered.
